newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rise in EU tapioca imports to pressure 1997 prices.
newsitem.headline: Rise in EU tapioca imports to pressure 1997 prices.

text.p: Vessel arrival lists show that some 500,000 tonnes of tapioca will arrive at northwest European ports from Thailand in the next three months, a total likely to pressure prices in Europe, trade sources said on Thursday.
"It looks like a big total and the surplus of tapioca we'll have in the market will cause prices to come down next year," said analyst Arie van Dijk of market statisticians Stigevo.
He said he expected the large volume to accelerate a price downturn in tapioca, also weakened by a forecast slide in grain prices during 1997, dented by oversupply in Europe.

Nearby tapioca now trades around 21.00 marks per 100 kilos but Van Dijk said his price forecast for the first half of next year was between 19 and 20 marks, falling to 18 to 19 marks in the second half of the year as the grain price weakened.
The reasons behind the large tonnage due are a combination of shipment timings and changes to the quota system operated by the Thailand, the world's top exporter, European traders said.

Some vessels have been delayed, while more distant arrivals appear, at least for now, to be on schedule. More Thai material was also being diverted to northern Europe because of the abundance of grain in Mediterranean countries, Van Dijk added.

In addition, the Thai authorities have tightened up their quota system, although tapioca pellet exports to Europe still have an annual ceiling at 5.50 million tonnes as part of an agreement with the EU to ship 21 million tonnes over four years.

Traders said up until now Thai shipments were more or less evenly spread over the year and any tapioca shipper who did not make exports in time, could roll the quota over. However, changes to the system now mean if a shipper fails to export, it loses that quota, they added.

Last week the Thai Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee announced the liberalisation of the local system for making tapioca exports to the EU, saying the current managed system made Thai tapioca less competitive compared to grains.
